review_notes:
I read all 313 lines of the target file. I grepped the `lean` tree for uses of `phaseBelt`, `exists_bounds_cutoff_and_phase`, `norm_fderiv_angularAmbient_le_at` and both uniform-bound theorems, and checked the definitions of `SphereAmbient` and `StandardSphere2` in Definitions.lean. Only the sphere-only theorem `exists_uniform_angular_bound` qualifies as an unnecessarily specialised statement. The file already has a general version for compact sets, `exists_uniform_angular_bound_on_compact`. That version does not depend on the sphere-only theorem or its helpers, so it can replace them. The proposed replacement proof has not been compiled. It relies on `angular k x` unfolding by definition to `angularAmbient k x.1`; if `exact` does not unfold it, adding `simpa [angular] using` fixes this.

Other candidates I considered and rejected:
- Widening `{n : ℕ∞}` to `WithTop ℕ∞`, so the smoothness lemmas also cover the analytic order ω. Nothing in the project needs ω here.
- Removing the `horizontal x ≠ 0` condition from `norm_fderiv_angularAmbient_le_at` or `contDiffAt_phase`. It is needed, because `phase` is not differentiable where `horizontal x = 0`.
- The specific heights -4/5 and 1/2 in the vanishing lemmas. They come from the support of the imported cutoff function, so they are not an arbitrary specialisation.
- `phase_eq_of_positive_scale`. It is already stated at a reasonable level of generality.

findings.declaration: exists_uniform_angular_bound (with its helper set phaseBelt, isCompact_phaseBelt, horizontal_ne_zero_on_phaseBelt, exists_bounds_cutoff_and_phase)
findings.excerpt:
theorem exists_uniform_angular_bound :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (k : ℕ) (x : StandardSphere2),
      ‖angular k x‖ + ‖fderiv ℝ (angularAmbient k) x.1‖ ≤ C * (1 + (k : ℝ)) := by
findings.problem: This theorem states the uniform C¹ bound only for points of the unit sphere. To prove it, the file builds a separate sphere-specific setup (lines 120–158): the set `phaseBelt`, its compactness proof, a nonvanishing lemma and `exists_bounds_cutoff_and_phase`. Grep shows nothing else uses these helpers. The general version, `exists_uniform_angular_bound_on_compact` (lines 240–278), proves the same bound for any compact `K ⊆ regularDomain`, and its proof is independent of the sphere-only one. The unit sphere is compact (`isCompact_sphere`) and lies in `regularDomain` (`sphere_mem_regularDomain`), so the sphere-only theorem is just one case of the general one, proved a second time with nearly the same argument.
findings.proposed_change:
Move the theorem below `exists_uniform_angular_bound_on_compact` and derive it from that theorem. Keep the statement unchanged:

theorem exists_uniform_angular_bound :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (k : ℕ) (x : StandardSphere2),
      ‖angular k x‖ + ‖fderiv ℝ (angularAmbient k) x.1‖ ≤ C * (1 + (k : ℝ)) := by
  obtain ⟨C, hC, h⟩ := exists_uniform_angular_bound_on_compact
    (isCompact_sphere (0 : SphereAmbient) 1) (fun x hx => sphere_mem_regularDomain ⟨x, hx⟩)
  exact ⟨C, hC, fun k x => h k x.1 x.2⟩

This works because `angular k x` is defined as `angularAmbient k x.1`. If the definition does not unfold automatically, use `simpa [angular] using h k x.1 x.2`. Then delete `phaseBelt`, `isCompact_phaseBelt`, `horizontal_ne_zero_on_phaseBelt` and `exists_bounds_cutoff_and_phase`, which are used only by the old proof. The theorem is also unused elsewhere, so deleting it outright is another option. Nothing degenerate needs a separate case: the sphere is nonempty, and the general theorem already handles points outside its height band (-4/5 to 1/2) by using that the derivative vanishes there.
findings.benefit: The file keeps a single general bound, valid on any compact subset of the regular domain, and drops about 45 lines of duplicated compactness and bound-extraction code. The sphere statement stays available as a two-line special case, so the two versions can no longer drift apart. Readers can also see that the sphere bound is just the general bound applied to the sphere.
